correctness.rationale: A real interval of length 2T meets at most floor(2T)+1 consecutive integers, and any full integer block at that width is achievable. Fixing a column containing a coordinate whose entire block has absolute value >= width makes its determinant-one complementary column unique, by the integer multiple description of Bezout solutions; this bounds such remote boxes by width squared. The finite verifier enumerates every remaining 4-tuple of block starts for widths 2,3,4,5 and returns exact maxima 6,20,36,60, all larger than width squared. All eight maximizing five-block patterns are checked, and every coordinate boundary value is used, forcing exact integral real centres for radius two; the 60 versus 52 counts are directly checked. The proof has exact quantifiers, closed-endpoint cases, and no inferred infinite conclusion.

originality.rationale: The closest inspected new primary paper proves large-box asymptotic upper bounds uniform over centre, rather than sharp small-box constants and equality centres. The classical fixed-determinant arbitrary-box work cited in that paper supplies general upper bounds, and a standard sequence gives only a single fixed nonnegative-coordinate cube. The claim that radius two has maximum 60, eight exact real maximizing centres and a smaller origin count of 52 is not an implication of those results. Actual title/alias/parameter and published-record queries did not identify equal or stronger local classifications. Residual historical priority is explicitly acknowledged.

value.rationale: The new uniform arbitrary-centre asymptotic counting problem naturally raises a finite-scale extremal question at the first complete integer radii. The theorem gives the entire initial transition profile, an exact complete equality-centre classification at the first radius with a centre shift advantage, and a concrete failure of extrapolating origin-centred extremality from centred counting formulae (60 versus 52). These are intrinsic quantities for integer symplectic/SL2 boxes and useful benchmarks for sharp constant studies, not a parameter-renaming or an arbitrary unmotivated slice. No larger-radius theorem is claimed.
